hook: Two AI assistants got popped this week for completely different reasons — Copilot leaked a secret parameter, Grok fell for an encrypted prompt-injection trick.
angle: Use both incidents to argue that 'the vendor secures the model' is not a security strategy — walk through what independent threat modeling and egress controls should look like for any LLM integration handling sensitive data.

hook: OpenAI just reaffirmed Zero Data Retention while a new study found frontier labs still won't say how they'd contain a rogue model.
angle: Contrast vendor data-handling promises with the containment gap — practical guidance for healthcare/finance architects on what to demand contractually versus what to build themselves (sandboxing, kill-switches, network isolation).

hook: GitHub's new 'canvases' make agentic workflows visible and steerable mid-run — which is exactly the control regulated teams have been missing.
angle: Break down how visible, steerable agent execution (plus GitHub's agent apps wiring into existing delivery workflows) gives architects a concrete pattern for human-in-the-loop governance instead of black-box automation.

hook: GitHub studied 50 open source projects and confirmed what maintainers already feared: most contributions are AI-first now, and review processes haven't caught up.
angle: Translate the maintainer-side lessons into an internal dependency-risk checklist — what to ask about a library's AI-contribution and review practices before pulling it into a regulated codebase.

hook: Microsoft just published an ROI framework for agent pilots — right as Gartner named Azure a Leader for cloud-native application platforms.
angle: Combine the two to make the case that Azure's platform investments (container/app runtime + agent economics tooling) are converging into a more measurable, defensible path from pilot to production than ad hoc agent experiments.
